facts.fact: According to eMarketer, only 8% of businesses said they were prepared for the CCPA.
facts.quote: According to [eMarketer](https://content-na1.emarketer.com/very-few-us-businesses-are-ccpa-ready?ecid=nl1009) only 8% of businesses said they are prepared.

facts.fact: CCPA was due to come into effect in January 2020.
facts.quote: CCPA is due to come into effect in January 2020, and will alter the relationship between publishers and consumers

facts.fact: Under CCPA, responsible parties have 30 days to respond to a consumer request, whereas under GDPR they have 40 days.
facts.quote: Responsible parties have 30 days to respond to a request Responsible parties have 40 days to respond to a request

facts.fact: Under CCPA, companies in breach can be fined up to $2500 per violation or $7500 per intentional violation.
facts.quote: Companies in breach can be fined up to $2500 per violation or $7500 per intentional violation

facts.fact: Under GDPR, companies in breach can be fined up to 4% of annual global revenue or 20 million euros.
facts.quote: Companies in breach can be fined up to 4% of their annual global revenue or 20 million euros

facts.fact: GDPR requires opt-in consent, whereas CCPA only requires an opt-out mechanism.
facts.quote: GDPR requires opt-in consent, whereas CCPA will only require the opt-out mechanism.

facts.fact: CCPA will create 3 categories of coverage: business, service provider, and third parties.
facts.quote: CCPA will create 3 categories of coverage: business, service provider, third parties.

facts.fact: The common fear around CCPA concerns an avalanche of 49 other state-level processes.
facts.quote: The common fear of CCPA is regarding the avalanche of 49 other state-level processes.

facts.fact: StackAdapt reports that 15 other states, such as Washington, Nevada, and Texas, are looking to implement privacy changes.
facts.quote: 15 other states such as Washington, Nevada, and Texas are also looking to implement changes

facts.fact: New York would be the second state to implement a state-level comprehensive privacy law under the New York Privacy Act, which would allow individual residents to file lawsuits.
facts.quote: Under NYPA, any resident of New York will have the ability to file an individual lawsuit against breaching companies

facts.fact: CCPA grants California residents rights including the right to opt out of the sale of their personal information and to receive equal service and price even if they exercise privacy rights.
facts.quote: Opt-out of the sale of their personal information. Receive equal service and price, even if they exercise their privacy rights.
